prompt:
A high-fidelity flat UI design mockup of a desktop web application screen, rendered straight-on with no perspective, no device frame, no hands, no room. This is a screen design, not a photograph or poster.

LAYOUT SKELETON, top to bottom, stated literally. The critical structural rule: the three month columns of the upper black band and the three month blocks of the lower grid are VERTICALLY ALIGNED on the same axes, sharing the same left edges and the same separating hairlines, so the whole screen reads as one continuous set of three month columns.

1. A full-width horizontal navigation beam, 56px tall, solid near-black carbon (#17161a). At its left the wordmark "PLIA" in condensed uppercase sans; beside it three small uppercase labels "TABLEAU DE BORD", "TRANSACTIONS", "HISTORIQUE" with the last underlined by a 2px red rule. At its right two thin line icons and a circular avatar initial.

2. On a warm light concrete-grey ground (#e6e3df) with faint concrete grain: a row of three small square account tabs with 45-degree cut corners, the first one filled black.

3. UPPER BAND, full width, about one fifth of the screen height: a dark carbon plate (#17161a) with 45-degree cut corners. At its far left, a narrow spine column matching the width of the grid's spine below, holding only a small uppercase letterspaced monospace label "OÙ TU ATTERRIS" in mid grey. To its right, THREE month columns separated by 1px hairlines in lighter carbon. Each column holds the month name in large condensed sans in off-white ("JUILLET", "AOÛT", "SEPTEMBRE") with the year "2026" in small monospace, and beneath it three stacked figures, each a tiny uppercase monospace label above a large monospace amount: "RÉEL 1 830,20 €", "PRÉVU 2 813,00 €", "SI DÉPASSEMENT −240,50 €" with the negative one in signal red. The third column carries a tiny uppercase monospace tag "PROJECTION".

4. LOWER GRID, full width, the remaining three quarters: ONE single dense table on a light plate (#eeece8) with 45-degree cut corners.
   - A single wide left spine column, same width and same left edge as the band's spine above, holding section band titles and expense category names in condensed sans, each with a small chevron and a tiny uppercase letterspaced monospace duration label beneath. Names read: "Salaire", "Loyer", "Assurance", "Courses", "Essence", "Sorties", "Abonnements", "Vacances".
   - To its right, THREE month blocks whose vertical hairlines line up exactly with the band's hairlines above. Each block is headed by a row of SIX tiny uppercase letterspaced monospace column labels: "BUDGET  DÉPENSÉ  BALANCE  RÉEL  PRÉVU  SI DÉP.". The month name is NOT repeated here — it lives in the band above. Inside each month block, a slightly stronger 1px hairline separates the first three columns (BUDGET DÉPENSÉ BALANCE) from the last three (RÉEL PRÉVU SI DÉP.), and the last three sit on a slightly deeper grey wash than the first three, because they are a running balance column that reads top to bottom like a column of arithmetic.
   - Rows organised into labelled horizontal bands running across the whole table: "CE QUI RENTRE" on a very faint carbon wash, "DÉPENSES PRÉVUES" and "DÉPENSES NON PRÉVUES" on a faint red wash, "PAS ENCORE RANGÉ".
   - At the bottom, THREE heavy total rows on a dark carbon wash with off-white numbers, reading in this order: "TOTAL DU MOIS", "SOLDE FIN DE MOIS", "TOTAL DÉPASSEMENT". The "SOLDE FIN DE MOIS" row is the heaviest of the three, solid black, its amounts larger than the rest of the table.
   - Every number monospace, tabular, right-aligned, format "1 830,20 €". Five or six numbers in signal red (#b31d25) for negatives. One row carries a small solid black pill chip with tiny white uppercase text "DÉPASSEMENT".

VISUAL WORLD, fixed and non-negotiable: absolutely no rounded corners anywhere; every panel corner is cut at 45 degrees. No drop shadows, no gradients, no glass, no glow. Depth comes only from 1px hairline rules (#c7c3bd) and flat tonal washes. Palette strictly: warm concrete grey ground, lighter plate, near-black carbon, mid grey #6b6966 for labels, and exactly one accent, a signal red #d7262e, used only for negative amounts and overspend marks. No green, no amber, no blue. Typography: condensed grotesque sans for names and headings, monospace for every number and every tiny uppercase label. No charts, no pie graphs, no gauges, no sparklines, no illustrations, no icons beyond thin line chevrons. Matte, precise, engineering-drawing calm.
